text: The Computer Science Students at SLIIT are planning to design a database to produce music albums. The students have come up with the following requirements. The students who have talent in music (i.e. singing, playing an instrument, etc..) are named as student musician. All student musicians are capable of singing songs. In addition, some of them play instruments and some of them act as producers when albums are produced. For each student musician a unique identification number, name and address are recorded. For those who play instruments, their specialization, and the duration that they play should be stored. For each instrument, a unique identification number and the name (e.g., guitar, violin, flute, etc.) are recorded. Each student capable of playing instruments may play several instruments, and a given instrument is played by one student. A student who plays instruments may supervise several other such students. Each album has a unique identification number, title, copyright date and a format (e.g., CD or MC). Each album has one student who acts as its producer. A student may produce several albums. Each album has several songs on it and a song appears on one album. The date that the songs are recorded on the album should be known. For each song a unique identification number, the title and the author are recorded. Each song is sung by one or more students, and a student sings several songs. The number of times that a song is sung should be recorded. Each song may have several melody types. For each melody type, the tempo, and the key for that song (e.g. C major, D minor etc.) are recorded. Different songs may have the same key.

subquestions.text: What are the entities that could be used for the above requirements?
Identify suitable attributes and the primary key, if any, for each of the entities that you have identified.
Is there a recursive relationship? Justify your answer.
Is there any weak entity type? Justify your answer.
Identify a likely superclass/subclass relationship. Justify your answer.

Construct a suitable EER diagram for the above given requirements. State any assumptions you make. Note: You may avoid showing the attributes on the entity types, but any attributes on the relationships must be shown.

text: Consider the following relational database schema containing airline flight information. Here the passenger relation gives the details of the passengers who book flights. The agency relation keeps the details of agent who books a flight for a passenger. The flight relation stores the details of each available flight. The booking relation stores required booking details. passenger (pid, pname, pgender, pcity) agency (aid, aname, acity) flight (fid, fdate, time, departs, arrives) booking (pid, aid, fid, fdate)

subquestions.text: Express each of the following queries as expressions in relational algebra.
Find the name of the agencies, such that they are located in the same city as passenger with passenger id 123.
Find the passenger names for those who do not have any bookings in any flights.
Get the details of flights that are scheduled on both dates 01/12/2024 and 02/12/2024 at 16:00 hours.
Retrieve the names of the passengers who have booked all available flights.
How many passengers have booked the flight f001?
Express the above queries (i) to (iv) in tuple calculus.
